+unattended-upgrades can keep a Debian testing system continuously up

+<node>

+    <!--

+
+      Request to postpone the pending upgrade.

+      The request is to be considered accepted unless the method
+      returns an error.
+    -->
+    <method name="Postpone"/>
+
+    <!--
+      AboutToStart:
+      @info: Information about the pending upgrade
+
+      The upgrade is about to start, but the user may postpone it.
+      Only gets emitted if the upgrade can be postponed.
+
+      The following fields may be included in the info:
+      <variablelist>
+        <varlistentry>
+          <term>postpone-timeout-time u</term>
+          <listitem><para>
+            Amount of time available for sending a valid Postpone request,
+            in seconds
+          </para></listitem>
+        </varlistentry>
+        <varlistentry>
+          <term>postpone-remaining-days u</term>
+          <listitem><para>
+            Number of days left until the upgrade cannot be postponed anymore,
+            and will be forced to run.
+          </para></listitem>
+        </varlistentry>
+    -->
+    <signal name="AboutToStart">
+        <arg name="info" type="a{sv}"/>
+    </signal>
+
+    <!--
+      Started:
+

+    -->
+    <signal name="Started"/>
+
+    <!--

+
+      The upgrade has finished
+    -->
+    <signal name="Finished"/>
+
+    <!--

+unattended-upgrades (2.14) unstable; urgency=medium
+
+  [ Fabio Fantoni ]
+  Unattended-Upgrade::Package-Whitelist works again in the default,
+  non-strict mode. Since version 1.16 it was silently ignored, and
+  every package from an allowed origin was upgraded unless
+  Unattended-Upgrade::Package-Whitelist-Strict was also set.
+
+  Systems with a Package-Whitelist will now only upgrade the listed
+  packages and their dependencies, as documented. If the unrestricted
+  upgrades were relied upon, remove or widen the whitelist, otherwise
+  security updates for packages not on the list will no longer be
+  installed.
+
+  If Package-Whitelist-Strict, or a Package-Blacklist of everything
+  but the wanted packages, was only a workaround for this bug, a plain
+  whitelist can be used again: it also upgrades the dependencies of
+  the listed packages.
+
+  "unattended-upgrades --dry-run --verbose" shows which packages
+  would now be upgraded.
+
+  [ Johan Walles ]
+  Upgrades now also run on battery power, as long as the average charge
+  of the batteries is at least 40%. Before, they only ran on AC power.
+  To keep the old behaviour, set
+  Unattended-Upgrade::MinBatteryLevel "ac-only".
+  Systems that set Unattended-Upgrade::OnlyOnACPower are not affected.
+
